screenwriter.name: Characters
screenwriter.definition: The people of the story: distinctive, many-layered personalities with clear goals they act on, who change over the story and whose relationships convince.

facets.name: Distinctive And Vivid
facets.meaning: Characters stand out as individuals, each unlike the others and unlike a type, rather than stereotypes or tropes.

facets.name: Depth And Emotional Core
facets.meaning: Characters are rounded and many-layered, with emotional complexity, contradictions and an emotional core a reader recognises as human.

facets.name: Goals, Stakes And Action
facets.meaning: Main characters want something clearly, have something at stake, and act on it, so they drive the story instead of being carried by it.

facets.name: Consistent And Credible
facets.meaning: Characters behave in keeping with who they are, scene to scene and episode to episode, so what they do is believable rather than convenient.

facets.name: Change Over The Story
facets.meaning: The central character (or several, in an ensemble) changes over the story, at a pace the story sets, through milestones the outline can name.

facets.name: Relationships Between Characters
facets.meaning: How characters bear on one another: convincing relationships, their interplay, and how those relationships develop.

screenwriter.name: Dialogue
screenwriter.definition: The words characters speak: natural and believable, in a voice each character owns, saying little, showing who they are and moving the story.

facets.name: Natural And Believable
facets.meaning: Lines sound like real people talking and behaving, so a reader believes them.

facets.name: A Voice For Each Character
facets.meaning: Each character speaks in a way of their own, so who is talking is plain without the name.

facets.name: Reveals Character
facets.meaning: What people say, and how, shows who they are.

facets.name: Moves The Story
facets.meaning: Dialogue does dramatic work, building the plot and creating tension, conflict or comedy, with no talk that has no purpose in the story.

facets.name: Succinct
facets.meaning: Lines say what they must in few words.

facets.name: Subtext Over Statement
facets.meaning: Characters do not announce what they feel; feeling comes through action and what lies beneath the line, built on what the characters want and what the story is about.

facets.name: Fits The Tone And World
facets.meaning: The way people speak suits the story's tone and setting and stays consistent from scene to scene.

screenwriter.name: Structure
screenwriter.definition: The framework of the story: how its acts, sequences and scenes are built and ordered so the story progresses from a beginning that starts on time to the climax and ending it builds to.

facets.name: The Story's Framework
facets.meaning: The frame the story is built on, three acts or another progression, used so the story advances effectively.

facets.name: Beginning, Middle And End
facets.meaning: The story holds together as a whole: a strong beginning, middle and end, coherent even when told out of order.

facets.name: Starting On Time
facets.meaning: The story gets into motion early, reaching its inciting incident before setup buries it, and hooks the reader in the opening pages.

facets.name: Climax And Ending
facets.meaning: The story builds to a climax and a satisfying ending that brings it full circle, not one that feels rushed.

facets.name: Scenes That Earn Their Place
facets.meaning: Each scene and sequence is built to move the story to the next, entering late and leaving early, with no superfluous scenes.

facets.name: Pace
facets.meaning: The timing of the action, of what is revealed and of character development, so the story neither drags nor rushes.

facets.name: Built For Its Form
facets.meaning: The story is shaped for what it is: a feature, a pilot or episode, or a short; for a series, a framework meant to repeat each episode.

screenwriter.name: Plot
screenwriter.definition: What happens: the actions, events, conflicts and turning points that propel the story forward in cause and effect, unfolding in ways the reader does not predict.

facets.name: Cause And Effect
facets.meaning: The actions and events of the story follow from one another, each turning point caused, so the chain leads to the ending.

facets.name: Conflict That Propels
facets.meaning: Forces in opposition, external or internal, give the story urgency and push it forward.

facets.name: Escalations, Revelations And Reversals
facets.meaning: The turning points that progress the story: problems that raise the stakes, new information that shifts a goal, and reversals of direction and power.

facets.name: Unpredictable Unfolding
facets.meaning: How the story unfolds surprises the reader: original, not predictable, not the standard formula.

facets.name: The Pull Of The Story
facets.meaning: The plot raises a dramatic question that makes the reader want to know what happens next and keep reading, taken on a journey.

facets.name: Goals And Stakes
facets.meaning: What the characters want and what is at risk if they fail, which gives the events their weight.

facets.name: Storylines Across A Series
facets.meaning: In series work, how the plot progresses over a season in arcs and episode storylines, and how storylines are restructured or added.

screenwriter.name: Theme
screenwriter.definition: What the story is about beneath its events: an underlying message revealed through plot, dialogue and image, clear and rich, and about something worth discussing.

facets.name: Underlying Message
facets.meaning: What the story is about beneath its events, revealed through its plot, its dialogue and its images.

facets.name: About Something
facets.meaning: The themes provoke thought, in any genre: the story is about something that might spark discussion.

facets.name: Clear And Rich
facets.meaning: The theme is clear and rich, centred on meanings that engage the writer, and it is where an audience's deeper investment comes from.

facets.name: Dramatised Through Character
facets.meaning: The theme is carried by what the characters go through, not stated: the characters embody the subject and their trajectory dramatises it.

facets.name: Thematic Unity
facets.meaning: The world, the structure and the ending hold to one set of meanings, the ending bringing the theme full circle.

screenwriter.name: Premise
screenwriter.definition: The idea behind the story, what it is about and its hook: a specific dramatic problem, original and strong enough to start the story forward and to hold up when developed.

facets.name: The Hook
facets.meaning: The idea behind the story, what it is about, strong enough to make someone want to read it and to start the movie forward by itself.

facets.name: Original Premise
facets.meaning: The premise is new, or an original take on a familiar story, set against what has already been made.

facets.name: A Dramatic Problem
facets.meaning: The premise sets out a specific problem: when something happens, someone has to do something, or else.

facets.name: Tested And Dramatically Viable
facets.meaning: The core concept has dramatic potential and holds up when developed; a flawed concept no amount of drafting fixes, and execution must deliver on it.

facets.name: A Premise That Sustains A Series
facets.meaning: For a series, a premise or general story line distinct from any one episode's story, able to generate many episodes.

screenwriter.name: Setting
screenwriter.definition: Where and when the story happens and the world it builds: its place and time, its rules and pressures, brought to life authentically and with texture.

facets.name: Place And Time
facets.meaning: Where and when the story takes place: its locale and period, and the sense of place it gives.

facets.name: A World With Rules And Pressures
facets.meaning: The storyworld is defined: its rules, what can and can't happen, its groups and beliefs, and the pressures it puts on every character.

facets.name: Authentically Brought To Life
facets.meaning: The world is rendered realistically and credibly, true to the people and places it represents.

facets.name: Pulls The Audience In
facets.meaning: The world draws an audience in and holds them there.

facets.name: Texture And Atmosphere
facets.meaning: The feel of the world on the page: its texture, atmosphere and tone, and speech that fits it.

facets.name: A World That Sustains A Series
facets.meaning: In series work the world is the returnable element, the engine of many stories, and must be dramatically or comedically sustainable.

screenwriter.name: Visual Storytelling
screenwriter.research: An ability to tell a story using images and sounds
screenwriter.definition: Telling the story in images and sounds: writing what can be seen and heard, showing rather than telling, so a director and crew can picture the film.

facets.name: Images And Sounds
facets.meaning: The story is conceived and written in the language of the screen, as images and sounds, with its scenes built from actions described that way.

facets.name: Showing, Not Telling
facets.meaning: Feeling and character come through action, description, image and behaviour rather than being stated.

facets.name: Filmable On The Page
facets.meaning: The script gives the director and production team something tangible to shoot, precise enough that they can picture the film, instead of reading like a novel.

facets.name: Cinematic Narrative
facets.meaning: The writing reads as cinema: a narrative that is distinct and cinematic and conveys the mood and feel of the film.

facets.name: Look And Feel
facets.meaning: The intended visual style and visual world of the project, expressed in the treatment and the bible as well as the script.

screenwriter.name: Distinctive Voice
screenwriter.definition: The writer's own way of seeing and telling, original and recognisably theirs, with something to say, so the script does not feel already read or seen.

facets.name: Original, Not Already Seen
facets.meaning: The script does not feel like something already read or seen: it rises above its genre and the standard formula.

facets.name: A Distinct Point Of View
facets.meaning: The story is told from the writer's own perspective, a singular angle on something human and truthful.

facets.name: Something To Say
facets.meaning: The writer has something to say and an artistic intention, a personal connection to the material that lets the voice reach an audience.

facets.name: Voice In The Storytelling
facets.meaning: The voice is on the page, in how the story is told: the scene description, the dialogue, the characters and the tone.

facets.name: Developed And Confident
facets.meaning: A voice is cultivated over time, honed through scripts and held with confidence.

screenwriter.name: Research
screenwriter.research: Conduct research to obtain factual information and authentic detail
screenwriter.definition: Conducting research to obtain factual information and authentic detail, using sources such as newspaper accounts, diaries, interviews, books and field observation, before and while writing.

facets.name: Documentary Research
facets.meaning: Reading books, articles, journals and records to gather the facts a subject needs.

facets.name: Research Method
facets.meaning: Choosing the research method a project needs and ranking the possible sources by how useful they are.

facets.name: Interviews And Fieldwork
facets.meaning: Interviewing people, scouting places and observing milieus so a world can be rendered realistically.

facets.name: Films, Books And Images
facets.meaning: Gathering reading, films and images that define the story's visual and sound world and enrich its characters.

facets.name: Authenticity
facets.meaning: Getting the people and the world right, so a reader can tell the writer knows what they are writing about.

facets.name: What Already Exists
facets.meaning: Knowing the films, series and other works on the same theme, so the script stays original and nothing is lifted from a classic.

screenwriter.name: Screenplay Format
screenwriter.definition: Laying out a script in the standard, agreed format: scene headings, action, character cues and dialogue on the page, 12-point Courier with correct margins, at a page count readers accept.

facets.name: Scene Headings And Action
facets.meaning: Scene headings in capitals naming interior or exterior, place and day or night, and action that shows only what is on screen.

facets.name: Character Cues And Dialogue
facets.meaning: Character names in capitals set toward the middle of the page, dialogue beneath them, parentheticals on their own line, and speeches broken across pages correctly.

facets.name: Font, Margins And Spacing
facets.meaning: 12-point Courier, correct margins and line spacing, with no cheating of margins to fit more pages.

facets.name: Page Count
facets.meaning: Keeping a script to the length its form and its readers accept: a feature roughly 80 to 125 pages, an hour of television roughly 40 to 70, a half hour 20 to 35.

facets.name: Spec Script, Not Shooting Script
facets.meaning: Leaving scene numbers, camera directions and most transitions out of a spec script; they belong to the shooting script made for production.

facets.name: Title Page And Submission
facets.meaning: Preparing the submission copy: a title page with one contact address, numbered pages, a single PDF, and no name anywhere when a contest reads anonymously.

facets.name: Spelling And Proofreading
facets.meaning: Clean spelling, punctuation, grammar and usage, proofread before the script goes out.

facets.name: Format For The Medium
facets.meaning: Using the format the medium dictates (film, filmed or taped TV drama, studio sitcom, radio, stage) and sending what each form asks for.

screenwriter.name: Writing
screenwriter.definition: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience: clear, engaging and concise, conveying feeling and emotion.

facets.name: Clarity
facets.meaning: Writing so others will understand: clear, concise, unambiguous.

facets.name: Economy Of Words
facets.meaning: Saying it in as few words as it takes, developing characters, relationships and several storylines in a concise format.

facets.name: Conveying Feeling
facets.meaning: Using description and dialogue to create suspense, tension, drama, comedy and conflict, so the reader feels it.

facets.name: Showing, Not Telling
facets.meaning: Showing feeling through action and description the camera can film, not stating it, and not writing like a novel.

facets.name: Texture Of Description
facets.meaning: Scene description written with a rich texture of its own.

facets.name: Quality Of Writing
facets.meaning: The overall strength of the writing on the page, judged apart from commercial potential.

facets.name: Audience And House Style
facets.meaning: Fitting the writing to its reader and, on a running show, to the show's house style.

screenwriter.name: Synopsis
screenwriter.definition: Summarising a story briefly to give a broad idea of the creative concept, in the short documents that carry it outside the screenplay: logline, synopsis, outline, treatment, scene breakdown, bible and pitch document.

facets.name: Logline
facets.meaning: One sentence, sometimes two, that holds the story's dramatic problem: when something happens, someone has to do something or else.

facets.name: Short Synopsis
facets.meaning: A paragraph giving genre and themes, the forces in opposition, goals and stakes, and the inciting incident.

facets.name: One-Page Synopsis
facets.meaning: The one-pager: the main pitch document, fleshing the dramatic question into characters, escalation, dilemmas and stakes, and for a feature the structure through to the ending.

facets.name: Outline
facets.meaning: A longer document (generally 4 to 12 pages) carrying the major plot and character turning points as escalations, revelations and reversals, in cause and effect.

facets.name: Treatment
facets.meaning: A 10 to 20 page present-tense telling of the film, scene by scene in order, confined to what a viewer would see and hear, conveying mood and tone.

facets.name: Scene Breakdown
facets.meaning: A scene-by-scene prose outline of the whole script without dialogue (the step outline or séquencier), checking every scene earns its keep.

facets.name: Series Bible
facets.meaning: The master document of a series: logline, one-pager, concept and themes, storyworld, format, characters, episode summaries, look and feel, about 10 to 15 pages.

facets.name: Pitch Document
facets.meaning: A short written presentation of a project's concept and nature, used to sell it; once asked for in writing, the WGA counts it as a treatment, story or format.

facets.name: Statement Of Intent
facets.meaning: The note that argues for the project and the writer's connection to it, for producers, directors, broadcasters and funding panels.

facets.name: Scriptment
facets.meaning: A hybrid of treatment and script: prose summary with the key dialogue scenes written out in screenplay form.

screenwriter.name: Revision
screenwriter.definition: Revising written material, rewriting scripts often several times before a final version, to meet one's own standards and the needs of producers and directors while keeping the project's coherence.

facets.name: Rewrite
facets.meaning: Significant changes in plot, story line or the relationships of characters, going to the root of the drama.

facets.name: Polish
facets.meaning: Changes in dialogue, narration or action that stop short of a rewrite.

facets.name: Finding What To Rewrite
facets.meaning: Analysing one's own draft to find the lines of rewriting, through to the shooting version.

facets.name: Revising From Notes
facets.meaning: Rewriting in response to artistic, budget and technical notes, judged on the quality of the revised script.

facets.name: Keeping Coherence
facets.meaning: Producing a new version that keeps the original project's singularity and coherence, without superficial changes for their own sake.

facets.name: Drafts On Deadline
facets.meaning: Turning drafts around quickly and creatively, a first, second and third draft to agreed deadlines.

facets.name: Production Rewrites
facets.meaning: Revising the script in response to budget and casting decisions and solving script problems during the shoot.

facets.name: Knowing When A Draft Is Done
facets.meaning: The writer decides when a draft is finished and delivers it, rather than revising on and on for free.

screenwriter.name: Story Critique
screenwriter.definition: Reading a script, synopsizing it and evaluating its strengths and weaknesses (its story, characters, dialogue and world), then critiquing it constructively with ways to improve it.

facets.name: Synopsizing
facets.meaning: Summarising the material at the head of coverage: a thumbnail sketch of the story.

facets.name: Strengths And Weaknesses
facets.meaning: Weighing the pros and cons of the subject, story, characters, dialogue and visual and sound world.

facets.name: Dramaturgical Analysis
facets.meaning: Checking the story's coherence against the author's intention: acts, point of view, character construction, the audience's place.

facets.name: Judging Potential
facets.meaning: Estimating whether the material is worth developing or acquiring: its format, genre, audience and possible funders.

facets.name: Constructive Notes
facets.meaning: Turning the analysis into clear, respectful creative and structural notes with ways forward.

facets.name: Tracking Drafts
facets.meaning: Once a project is in development, comparing drafts to track changes, note improvements and suggest next steps.

facets.name: Breadth Of Reference
facets.meaning: Knowing films and scripts of every genre and period, bad ones included, to see how the page becomes the screen.

screenwriter.name: Critical Thinking
screenwriter.definition: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems, and thinking through new concepts well enough to convey them in writing.

facets.name: Weighing Alternatives
facets.meaning: Identifying the strengths and weaknesses of the possible approaches and choosing the most appropriate.

facets.name: Solving Complex Problems
facets.meaning: Identifying a complex problem, reviewing what bears on it, and developing and evaluating options.

facets.name: Grasping New Concepts
facets.meaning: Thinking through or understanding new concepts, and conveying them through writing.

facets.name: Evaluating Own And Others' Work
facets.meaning: Judging the aims, success or failure of one's own scripts and others'.

facets.name: Analytical Ability
facets.meaning: Analytical ability with an awareness of structure, and a gift for observation and reflection.

screenwriter.name: Innovation
screenwriter.definition: A tendency to be inventive, imaginative and to adopt new perspectives: coming up with unusual or clever ideas and new plots, characters and ways of doing things.

facets.name: Inventiveness
facets.meaning: Being inventive and imaginative, coming up with new ways of doing things.

facets.name: Original Ideas
facets.meaning: Unusual or clever ideas, and new and interesting plots, characters and stories, with unpredictable turns.

facets.name: Fund Of Ideas
facets.meaning: Having many ideas to hand, the number counting more than their quality.

facets.name: Beyond The Formula
facets.meaning: Rising above the genre and the standard formula, so the script presents a unique perspective rather than a cookie-cutter one.

facets.name: Creative Risk
facets.meaning: Taking risks in form and narrative approach, experimenting, and risking failure to succeed.

screenwriter.name: Time Management
screenwriter.definition: Managing one's own time and the time of others, following a work schedule so drafts and story documents are delivered on agreed deadlines.

facets.name: Meeting Deadlines
facets.meaning: Delivering drafts, rewrites and story documents on the dates agreed.

facets.name: Planning The Writing
facets.meaning: Organising a commission's stages (synopsis, treatment, step outline, script) and the writing schedule with rigour.

facets.name: Realistic Timelines
facets.meaning: Setting timelines one can keep and keeping producers and executives updated along the way.

facets.name: Several Projects At Once
facets.meaning: Working on several projects simultaneously, on long film timescales and shorter television ones.

facets.name: Prolific Output
facets.meaning: Producing a high volume of pages.

screenwriter.name: Perseverance
screenwriter.definition: Determination and resolve to complete tasks in the face of difficult circumstances, on projects that can take years, holding up when problems come.

facets.name: Determination
facets.meaning: Persisting and staying determined through obstacles.

facets.name: Seeing Long Projects Through
facets.meaning: Completing complex projects that can take years.

facets.name: Resilience
facets.meaning: Holding up when problems and difficulties come.

facets.name: Self-Discipline
facets.meaning: Driving one's own work with self-discipline and personal motivation.

screenwriter.name: Taking Notes
screenwriter.definition: Taking feedback from producers, script editors and peers constructively and without defensiveness, finding the problem behind each note, and answering it with comprehensive solutions in the next draft.

facets.name: Listening And Clarifying
facets.meaning: Listening, asking for clarification, and answering a set of notes by saying which are clear and which need more.

facets.name: Openness Without Defensiveness
facets.meaning: Welcoming positive and negative feedback and responding constructively, clearly and respectfully.

facets.name: Diagnosing The Note
facets.meaning: Finding what is really causing the problem a note points at, and how best to treat it.

facets.name: Holding Your Take
facets.meaning: Not saying yes to every note: explaining why one doesn't work and arguing for creative decisions.

facets.name: Addressing Notes
facets.meaning: Acting on the notes: reconsidering the approach and carrying the answers into the next version.

facets.name: Seeking Feedback
facets.meaning: Getting feedback from producers, script editors, actors and everyone in the room, whatever their title.

screenwriter.name: Pitching
screenwriter.definition: Presenting your story ideas and screenplays to buyers (producers, film and television executives, agents and managers), aloud and in pitch documents, to win their interest.

facets.name: Preparing The Pitch
facets.meaning: Doing the homework before the room: learning the project's history, the competition and what the buyers want, reading the material, and rehearsing the pitch aloud against the clock.

facets.name: Presenting The Story Aloud
facets.meaning: Telling the story and its intentions out loud, briefly and in order, bringing out its strengths and what makes it singular, so the listener grasps it at once.

facets.name: The Take
facets.meaning: Finding what the story is really about, its core way in, and shaping a take that meets the buyers' expectations while feeling uniquely your own.

facets.name: Why You
facets.meaning: Showing what connects you to the material, so the buyer believes you are the writer for it.

facets.name: Pitch Documents
facets.meaning: The written side of a pitch: the pitch outline or document, the deck, the series bible and the statement of intent, and knowing that leaving such material behind unpaid is free work the MBA prohibits.

facets.name: Feedback On The Pitch
facets.meaning: Taking the listeners' feedback and questions on a pitch and working their notes into it rather than ignoring them.

screenwriter.name: Networking
screenwriter.definition: Reaching out to and meeting people in the industry, above all agents and producers, and building and keeping those relationships for mutual benefit.

facets.name: Meeting Agents And Producers
facets.meaning: Getting in front of the people who commission writing (agents, producers, directors, showrunners, broadcasters) in meetings, including the general meeting.

facets.name: Keeping In Touch
facets.meaning: Maintaining contacts over time: following up when invited to, keeping track of what people are doing, leaving every meeting with an open line, and not burning bridges.

facets.name: Fellow Writers
facets.meaning: A network among fellow writers and peers at the same level, met in rooms, roundtables and programmes, who lean on and recommend each other.

facets.name: Everyone In The Room
facets.meaning: Treating everyone you meet, whatever their title, as part of your network, since today's assistants become tomorrow's buyers.

facets.name: Festivals And Events
facets.meaning: Going to festivals, conferences and their events to meet the industry and put projects in front of it.

facets.name: Working Your Reps
facets.meaning: Using your agent or manager actively: telling them what you need, asking for introductions to their other clients and for submissions on projects.

screenwriter.name: Promotion
screenwriter.definition: Promoting your work and yourself as a writer to professionals and the public: getting scripts to producers and directors, talking about the work at events, festivals and readings, and finding new clients.

facets.name: Getting The Script Out
facets.meaning: Promoting an original screenplay to producers and directors and seeking backers and financial partners for it.

facets.name: Talking About The Work
facets.meaning: Talking about your work in public: at meetings, workshops and debates, in readings and speeches.

facets.name: Festivals
facets.meaning: Taking part in film festivals to promote projects.

facets.name: Publicity For The Film
facets.meaning: Taking part in the publicity of a produced film: the press junket, the press kit and the premiere, which the MBA gives the writer a right to.

facets.name: Getting Noticed
facets.meaning: Getting yourself noticed and finding new clients and readers: through competitions, social media and other writers and industry professionals, and by citing competition placements.

facets.name: Promotional Documents
facets.meaning: Writing the documents that sell a project to partners: the series bible as a promotion document, the pitch and the statement of intent.

screenwriter.name: Persuasion
screenwriter.definition: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior: arguing a creative point, influencing and winning people over, resolving differences in professional opinions and negotiating.

facets.name: Changing Minds
facets.meaning: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior, and convincing listeners to buy into an idea.

facets.name: Arguing A Creative Point
facets.meaning: Standing up for your creative choices: explaining respectfully why a note doesn't work, saying what matters most to you, and pitching what you think is best rather than what you think they want to hear.

facets.name: Winning People Over
facets.meaning: Influencing the people in the room, buyers and fellow writers alike, so they come on board with your idea and with you.

facets.name: Reaching Common Ground
facets.meaning: Bringing differing opinions together, as in a story meeting, and reconciling them into a common ground.

facets.name: Negotiating The Deal
facets.meaning: Negotiating your own deal, with your representatives, above the guild minimums: compensation, bonuses and other deal points.

screenwriter.name: Speaking
screenwriter.definition: Talking to others to convey information effectively, expressing ideas in speech, clearly, so others will understand.

facets.name: Getting Ideas Across
facets.meaning: Communicating information and ideas in speech so others understand them.

facets.name: Speaking Clearly
facets.meaning: Speaking clearly enough that others can understand you.

facets.name: In Meetings
facets.meaning: Speaking for yourself and your work with producers, executives, directors and your reps: presenting yourself and your projects, giving a coherent account of your intentions, and keeping communication open.

facets.name: Speaking To An Audience
facets.meaning: Giving a talk or presentation in which a piece of work or an idea is shown and explained to an audience, from a reading to a pitch on a stage.

screenwriter.name: Social Perceptiveness
screenwriter.definition: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

facets.name: Reading Reactions
facets.meaning: Noticing how others react and understanding why they react as they do.

facets.name: Reading Buyers
facets.meaning: Understanding why producers and executives want what they want, what pressures they are under, and what lies behind their notes.

facets.name: Reading The Audience
facets.meaning: Understanding how an audience, from readers to a pitch panel, reacts to certain ideas, so as to connect with it.

screenwriter.name: Film Production Process
screenwriter.definition: Knowing the stages of making a film or programme (scriptwriting, financing, shooting, editing and distribution), the trades the script passes through, and what it costs.

facets.name: Stages Of Production
facets.meaning: The development stages from script through financing, shooting and editing to distribution.

facets.name: Production Departments
facets.meaning: Camera, directing, design, costume, lighting, editing and sound, and how each trade meets the writer's job.

facets.name: What A Script Costs
facets.meaning: Knowing the financial impact of storylines, cast and effects, and estimating a budget to check the project is feasible.

facets.name: The Writer In Production
facets.meaning: Where the writer comes in once the script is made: meeting the director, the cast reading, the set, the cuts.
